Rung.Comment: "Sanity Check" Make sure that the sizes and other config values are correct
Clear the Random number "copy" that is being used in the fault generation - to ensure that the fault is really only triggered once Copy input Cfg_ data into approrpriate locations
If there are no faults to be generated, there is no need to continue with the code execution
Only generate random number every X milisecond

Calculate the "fraction" of [0-1] range for each fault = basically the "smallest step" to increment the limit interval only perform this recalculation once every "fault generation cycle"
1) Sum up all the individual "probability ratios" of all faults 2) check that the "Overall Fault Probability" is within the correct interval 3) calculate the "smallest incrementation step" used for setting comparison limits

Fault generation
1) compute the comparison limits 2) if the current random number is within the limits, generate the fault
The actual upper limit of the fault's random number will become lower limit in the next cycle of the loop
When the fault becomes active, set the Preset of the timer to a random value between Cfg_FaultDurationMin seconds and Cfg_FaultDurationMax seconds
When the fault is active, run the timer And disable the fault when a preset period elapses
Next iteration of the loop or exit
Make the last result of Random Number call available to the "outside" (might be useful for some other fault generation procedures)
